&reftitle.description;
intcurl_pause CurlHandlehandle intflags
Pause or unpause a cURL session, in either the read, write or both directions. This function itself has no special requirement to be called from any particular context: it works the same whether called from inside a transfer callback or from ordinary script code between two curl_multi_exec calls. What does require a callback is triggering the pause in the first place, by returning CURL_WRITEFUNC_PAUSE or CURL_READFUNC_PAUSE from a CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION or CURLOPT_READFUNCTION callback registered with curl_setopt.
If a transfer is paused this way during a plain curl_exec call (as opposed to the multi API), nothing but the paused callback itself could ever call curl_pause with CURLPAUSE_CONT to resume it, and it will not run again while paused. Unless another mechanism intervenes, such as CURLOPT_TIMEOUT or a CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION callback that itself calls curl_pause, curl_exec never returns.
The pause state is not cleared by curl_multi_remove_handle or by starting a new transfer on the handle: a handle paused with CURLPAUSE_RECV, then removed and re-run directly with curl_exec, opens a new connection but never returns, since the pause is still in effect. Only an explicit curl_pause call with CURLPAUSE_CONT, or curl_reset, lifts it.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns an error code (CURLE_OK for no error).
